question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about cell cycle?

options.text: In G2, phase cell prepare to divide.
The correct sequence of cell cycle is G1,S, G2, M.
DNA replication takes place in S cycle.

solution:
The correct answer is __**M is a meiosis phase**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ordered sequence of events that occur in a cell in preparation for cell division is called the cell cycle.
 
• The cell cycle is divided into two phases:
 
 
• Interphase
 
• M Phase
 
 
 
• **M phase** refers to the **mitotic phase** in the cell cycle, not meiosis.
 
• It involves the processes of mitosis (division of the nucleus) and cytokinesis (division of the cytoplasm), leading to two daughter cells.
 
• **Meiosis** is a specialized type of cell division occurring in germ cells, which is distinct from the regular cell cycle.
 
• The Interphase represents the phase between two successive M phases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Interphase is divided into three further phases;
 
 
• G1 Phase
 
• S Phase
 
• G2 Phase
 
 
 
• During the G1 phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. 
 
• S or Synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place
 
• During the G2 phase, proteins are synthesized in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20b251078149172c1b03f7d779402e459bab2398e8560645f0902597c44ed91d.png]
